conventions.convention: Fields use A(z)=Σ A_(n) z^(-n-1), with A_(n)v=0 for every sufficiently large n on each fixed vector. Formal Laurent series have support bounded below.
Locality uses ordinary commutators and a nonnegative integer exponent. The delta distribution is δ(z,w)=Σ z^(-n-1)w^n; the two iota expansions specify different formal expansions for negative powers.
A vertex algebra has a nonzero vacuum, T1=0, strong creation Y(a,z)1=e^(zT)a, translation covariance [T,Y(a,z)]=∂zY(a,z), and locality. Grading and conformal structure are additional data.
The affine algebra is the loop central extension without a degree derivation; [x_m,y_n]=[x,y]_(m+n)+mδ_(m,-n)B(x,y)K, with long roots of square 2.
The vacuum module is induced from g[t] acting by zero and K acting by arbitrary k∈C; its vacuum is 1⊗1.
The normalized Sugawara denominator is 2(k+h∨), and the formula is undefined at k=-h∨.

load_bearing.statement: For a complex vector space V with nonzero vacuum 1 and T1=0, a pairwise local family of translation-covariant fields satisfying A(z)1=e^(zT)a_A, whose negative-mode words together with 1 span V, extends uniquely to a vertex-algebra state–field map with Y(a_A,z)=A(z).
Multiplication induces a vector-space isomorphism U(g⊗t^(-1)C[t^(-1)]) → V^k(g), u↦u1. In particular, the vacuum is nonzero and ordered negative-current-mode monomials form a basis.

For every finite-dimensional complex simple g and k∈C, the current distributions on V^k(g) are creative, translation-covariant fields and satisfy [J^x(z),J^y(w)]=J^[x,y](w)δ(z,w)+kB(x,y)∂wδ(z,w), hence locality of order at most 2 and the displayed normalized current OPE.
D(K)=0 and D(x_n)=-n x_(n-1) define a Lie derivation preserving g[t]⊕CK and induce T on V^k(g) with T1=0 and [T,x_n]=-n x_(n-1).

For fields with locality order N≥0, their commutator has the unique expansion Σ_(j=0)^(N-1) C_j(w)∂w^jδ(z,w)/j!, where C_j(w)=Res_z((z-w)^j[A(z),B(w)]); the stated generalized-binomial mode commutator follows. For N=0 the sums are empty.

For finite-dimensional complex simple g and every k∈C, the induced module V^k(g) has a unique vertex-algebra structure with its specified vacuum and Y(x_(-1)1,z)=Σ x_n z^(-n-1). This includes critical levels and asserts no conformal vector, simple quotient, unitarity, or integrability.

concerns.concern: Step 1.1 proves that both mode sums are finite for fixed m,v and immediately concludes, “Thus every nth product of fields is again a field.” Finiteness establishes well-defined coefficients; lower truncation additionally requires their vanishing for sufficiently large m. This follows readily from the displayed formula: its first sum vanishes once m exceeds the cutoff for B on v, and its second sum involves only finitely many nonzero A_(j)v, on each of which B has a cutoff. That short argument is omitted.
